# The dataset

Long-read (Oxford Nanopore) single-nucleus RNA-seq of hiPSC-derived neurons
from the Duan lab — the same cells and donors as
[Liang et al., *Science* 392:eadw3949 (2026)](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adw3949),
assayed on Nanopore rather than the published 10x Multiome. Not itself
published.

```
data/NP184_NP187_NP188_combined_DUAN_21-0/   0 hr   27.5 GB
data/NP189_NP190_NP193_combined_DUAN_21-1/   1 hr   34.2 GB
data/NP191_NP192_NP194_combined_DUAN_21-6/   6 hr   36.4 GB
```

**Coculture batch 21, four donors, three KCl-stimulation timepoints
(0 / 1 / 6 h).** The three `NP` identifiers in each name are sequencing runs
(flow cells) of that one library — three per library, all distinct across the
three files.

Numbers below are **measured from the BAMs** unless tagged *[metadata]* (Table
S1 of the paper, or `cell_barcodes_w_meta.txt.gz`) or *[slides]* (the scNanoGPS
statistics we were sent).

# Headline numbers

| | 0 hr | 1 hr | 6 hr | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cell barcodes | 8,612 | 12,023 | 10,051 | **30,686** |
| Primary reads | 61.19 M | 75.62 M | 80.65 M | **217.46 M** |
| Cells with donor assignment | 4,866 | 7,891 | 6,625 | **19,382** |
| Reads in assigned cells | 31.76 M | 46.73 M | 50.57 M | **129.06 M** |

Four donors present at every timepoint, so the design is **paired within
donor across stimulation**.

# Per-library statistics

Full pass over every primary read in each library.

| | 0 hr | 1 hr | 6 hr |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cells | 8,612 | 12,023 | 10,051 |
| Primary reads | 61,189,011 | 75,617,929 | 80,650,873 |
| Total alignment records | 85,465,939 | 102,144,372 | 108,264,439 |
| Median UMIs / cell | 4,967 | 4,622 | 6,028 |
| Mean UMIs / cell | 7,105 | 6,289 | 8,024 |
| Mean read length | 617 bp | 610 bp | 627 bp |
| Median read length | 578 bp | 512 bp | 541 bp |
| % spliced | 19.45% | 20.17% | 19.87% |
| % no base quality | 20.81% | 16.16% | 19.15% |
| % chrM | 6.27% | 7.48% | 6.53% |

The three libraries are consistent — % spliced within 0.7
points, read length within 17 bp. So QC thresholds and pipeline settings
established on one apply to all three.

Read-length percentiles (100 k sample):

| | p10 | p25 | median | p75 | p90 | p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 hr | 306 | 412 | 578 | 776 | 1,005 | 2,044 |
| 1 hr | 276 | 353 | 512 | 753 | 1,049 | 2,110 |
| 6 hr | 273 | 367 | 541 | 773 | 1,054 | 2,128 |

**Always filter with `-F 0x900`.** Secondary alignments are 26–28% of records.

The BAMs are already **UMI-deduplicated** (1.01 reads per barcode-UMI pair at
0 hr), so primary reads ≈ unique molecules.

# Genomic origin of reads

Genome-wide, every primary read, using the **10x Cell Ranger definition** — the
field standard for 10x data:

> **Exonic** — ≥50% of the read's aligned bases fall within an exon
> **Intronic** — not exonic, but the read overlaps a gene body
> **Intergenic** — neither

"Aligned bases" means matched bases only (`M/=/X`). Soft-clips, insertions,
deletions and splice gaps are all excluded from the denominator — the last of
these matters, because otherwise every spliced read would be misclassified as
intronic. Annotation is the IsoQuant extended GTF.

| | 0 hr | 1 hr | 6 hr |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Exonic** | **36.48%** | **41.19%** | **39.21%** |
| **Intronic** | **57.02%** | **52.89%** | **55.34%** |
| **Intergenic** | 6.50% | 5.92% | 5.45% |
| Reads classified | 61,179,472 | 75,613,564 | 80,644,703 |

Restricted to the donor-assigned cells (the set used for all downstream
analysis):

| | 0 hr | 1 hr | 6 hr |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exonic | 34.64% | 39.36% | 37.44% |
| Intronic | 59.61% | 54.95% | 57.48% |
| Intergenic | 5.75% | 5.69% | 5.08% |
| Reads classified | 31,763,453 | 46,726,114 | 50,567,455 |

Three things worth knowing about these numbers:

* **The 50% threshold is not doing much work.** The distribution of exonic
  fraction per read is strongly bimodal — 64.5% of reads have *no* exonic bases
  at all and 24% are entirely exonic, with only 1.5% anywhere near the cut.
  Moving the threshold from 30% to 90% changes the exonic fraction by ~4 points.
  The result is a property of the data, not of the cutoff.
* **Intron dominance is a size effect, not a capture failure.** Exons are only
  ~9% of genic sequence, so a uniform library would be ~9% exonic. At 36–41%
  the data is ~4× exon-enriched; introns still win on read count because there
  is ~11× more intronic sequence.
* **Do not use chr21 as a proxy for this.** chr21 alone gives 29.0% exonic /
  65.0% intronic at 0 hr — 7–8 points off the genome-wide value, because it is
  unusually intron-heavy (345 lncRNA vs 190 protein-coding genes).

The 1 hr shift toward exonic (+4.7 points) and away from intronic (−4.1) is
consistent with post-stimulation transcript maturation, and the same shape
appears in the collaborators' independently computed QC numbers. Treat it as
suggestive until tested within donors — library-level differences in
nuclear/cytoplasmic capture would produce the same pattern.

Method detail, per-read exon structure and the 3′ bias:
[read structure](read_structure.html).

# Donor assignment

*[metadata]* Four donors, balanced 2 cases / 2 controls and 2 male / 2 female,
all European ancestry, coculture batch 21, sequencing batch 25.

| Donor | Sex | Diagnosis | Age | dbGaP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CD_21 | M | case | 29 | phs000167.v1.p1 |
| CD_31 | F | control | 29 | phs000021.v3.p2 |
| CD_36 | M | case | 57 | phs000021.v3.p2 |
| CD_48 | F | control | 72 | phs000167.v1.p1 |

## Cells per donor

| Timepoint | CD_21 | CD_31 | CD_36 | CD_48 | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 hr | 1,463 | 1,237 | 823 | 1,343 | 4,866 |
| 1 hr | 2,122 | 2,146 | 1,267 | 2,356 | 7,891 |
| 6 hr | 1,936 | 1,746 | 1,056 | 1,887 | 6,625 |
| **total** | **5,521** | **5,129** | **3,146** | **5,586** | **19,382** |

## Reads per donor (millions)

The four donor columns are the reads we can use. The last two columns are
totals, not additional groups:

* **assigned** = sum of the four donor columns — reads in cells that have a
  donor label from the mapping file
* **unassigned** = reads in cells with no donor label, which get discarded
* assigned + unassigned = the library's total primary reads

| Timepoint | CD_21 | CD_31 | CD_36 | CD_48 | assigned<br>(4 donors) | unassigned<br>(discarded) | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 hr | 9.30 | 7.47 | 6.25 | 8.75 | **31.76** | 29.42 | 61.19 |
| 1 hr | 12.66 | 12.35 | 7.85 | 13.87 | **46.73** | 28.89 | 75.62 |
| 6 hr | 14.97 | 13.22 | 8.44 | 13.93 | **50.57** | 30.08 | 80.65 |

Cells behind the unassigned column: 3,746 / 4,132 / 3,426.

CD_36 is consistently the smallest donor (~6–8 M reads); the others are
7–15 M. Every donor × timepoint sample has at least 6.2 M reads, which is
ample for per-sample isoLASER — the chr21 test run managed on 62–101 k.

## Coverage of the assignment

| Timepoint | BAM cells | Cell-line *[slides]* | % | Both line + type *[metadata]* | % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 hr | 8,612 | 5,035 | 58.46% | 4,866 | 56.50% |
| 1 hr | 12,023 | 8,097 | 67.35% | 7,891 | 65.63% |
| 6 hr | 10,051 | 6,911 | 68.76% | 6,625 | 65.91% |

The small gap (169 / 206 / 286 cells) is the cell-type filter: the mapping file
contains only `GABA`/`nmglut`/`npglut`, so it is the *intersection* of the
cell-line and cell-type calls. For allele-specific splicing only the donor
matters, so the unfiltered cell-line list would be slightly preferable.

Note 0 hr has a lower assignment rate (56.5%) than 1 hr and 6 hr (~66%) — the
unstimulated library had proportionally more cells failing QC.

# Platform and processing

| | |
|---|---|
| Sequencing | Oxford Nanopore |
| Chemistry | 10x Multiome / scARC — 16 bp cell barcode + 12 bp UMI |
| Pre-processing | **scNanoGPS** *[slides]* |
| Aligner | minimap2, spliced |
| Reference | GRCh38, 10x `refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A` |
| Strandedness | `--strand reverse` |
| Annotation | IsoQuant v3.3.0 (`OUT.extended_annotation.gtf`) |

Two scNanoGPS conventions differ from what single-cell tooling expects:

* the **cell barcode is in the `RG` tag**, not `CB`
* the **UMI is appended to the read name**, not in `UB`

```
QNAME  281b9c59-a0da-477b-84b9-d9895f6ec585_TTCAAGATATAT
RG:Z:  TTCGTTAGTACCAGGT
```

This is convenient for one thing: `samtools view -R <barcode_list>` splits a
BAM by donor directly, with no re-tagging.
